description: Passionate about technology, AI/ML, and space exploration. Looking for creative and dedicated teammates to innovate, collaborate, and build something extraordinary!
summary:
LunaNav is an intuitive, interactive lunar mission planning platform designed to solve the severe illumination and communication constraints of landing at the Moon’s South Pole. We developed a full-stack 3D application featuring a dynamic lunar globe with authentic albedo sampling and interactive pin-dropping, a 360° Polar SkyDome horizon-obstruction engine, ephemeris-driven Sun and Earth orbital tracking, solar power generation modeling, a multi-criteria site comparison matrix, and a physics-based autonomous descent simulator with hazard detection and tip-over dynamics.

LunaNav directly addresses the challenge by replacing complicated legacy ephemeris software with a streamlined, responsive visual interface. Mission planners and the public can quickly compare landing sites and calendar dates, visualizing real-time Sun and Earth positions against NASA LOLA topographic horizons to assess critical sunlight duty cycles and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows.

This is vital for Artemis-era exploration, where landing just meters away or timing arrival off by hours risks battery freeze in permanently shadowed regions. LunaNav bridges science and engineering, transforming complex lunar astrodynamics into accessible, actionable spatial intelligence for safe, sustainable exploration.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

  • LunaNav is a web-based lunar mission planning and ephemeris visualization platform designed for evaluating landing sites at the Moon's south pole.
  • It computes the real-time positions of the Sun and Earth relative to any candidate landing site on the Moon.
  • It integrates NASA LRO LOLA digital elevation models (DEMs) to generate a true 3D local horizon mask, determining whether towering crater rims block low-angle sunlight or obstruct Direct-to-Earth (DTE) radio communication.
  • It features an interactive 3D lunar globe with high-resolution albedo and bump textures, allowing users to explore candidate sites or drop custom pins with instant slope and elevation sampling.
  • It includes an Autonomous Landing and Hazard Avoidance (ALHAT) simulator that models descent trajectories from 4,200 meters down to touchdown, computing fuel consumption, thrust vectoring, slope tip-over limits, and obstacle avoidance.
  • It incorporates computer vision hazard detection on descent imagery to classify micro-craters, boulder fields, and permanently shadowed regions into an aggregate Safety Suitability Index.

What benefits does it have?

  • Unifies celestial mechanics, GIS terrain analysis, and landing dynamics into a single accessible interface, replacing fragmented legacy workflows.
  • Prevents mission planning errors caused by grazing polar sunlight by replacing flat-horizon approximations with true topographic obstruction calculations.
  • Provides rapid multi-site trade-offs, enabling teams to compare power generation potential, illumination windows, and communication passes simultaneously.
  • Delivers real-time landing safety validation, allowing planners to test whether an illuminated site is structurally safe for touchdown.
  • Highly accessible with zero installation required, running directly in modern web browsers across desktops, tablets, and mobile devices.

What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Accelerates mission planning for Artemis and commercial lunar lander (CLPS) teams by providing a rapid decision-support tool.
  • De-risks critical lunar surface missions by identifying terrain hazards and solar/RF eclipse cycles before flight commitment.
  • Democratizes planetary exploration data by translating complex NASA SPICE geometry and raw altimetry into intuitive visual tools for researchers, students, educators, and the public.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages: TypeScript, Python 3.11, and GLSL shader code.
  • Frontend Framework: React 18 with Vite for high-performance builds.
  • 3D Graphics & Visualization: Three.js and WebGL 2.0 for 3D planetary rendering, surface displacement, and descent physics particles.
  • Styling & UI Components: Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, and Recharts for telemetry and solar/comms window plotting.
  • Backend & Numerical Computing: FastAPI, NumPy, and SciPy for coordinate frame transformations and trajectory simulation.
  • Image & Raster Processing: Pillow (PIL) and PyVista for DEM elevation profile slicing and normal map generation.
  • Datasets: NASA LRO LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) DEMs, NASA LROC NAC imagery, and NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) south pole topographic models.
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub.

How is your project creative?

  • Integrates three historically separate disciplines—ephemeris calculation, topographic GIS mapping, and flight dynamics simulation—into a unified workflow.
  • Replaces static warning labels with active physics simulations, demonstrating dynamic tip-over crashes and landing strut collapses when landing on unsafe slopes or boulder fields.
  • Visualizes the invisible horizon, overlaying local crater rims directly on solar and Earth elevation charts to show exactly why communication and power windows open and close.
  • Features an interactive coordinate picker that dynamically extracts local topography, slope gradients, and landing zones anywhere on the 3D Moon.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Extreme South Pole lighting conditions, where the Sun circles the horizon at angles between 1.5° and 3.0°, creating elongated shadows and permanently shadowed craters.
  • Lunar libration cycles causing the Earth to oscillate by ±6° to 8° above and below local topographic horizons, driving intermittent communication dropouts.
  • Lander stability constraints, including center-of-mass height, landing strut footprint radius (0.6 m), maximum slope limit (10.5°), and vertical touchdown velocity limits.
  • Web performance optimization, converting multi-gigabyte raw altimetry rasters into edge-optimized 2K/4K displacement and normal maps for smooth browser rendering.
  • User experience and cognitive load, utilizing clear aerospace telemetry standards, color-coded hazard alerts, and responsive layouts across all device sizes.
